clue.text: It's difficult, with nothing in store

indicators.note: in tells us the zero for nothing is placed within the word for difficult

parts.note: something difficult is hard
nothing is zero, shown by the round letter O

explanation.surface: A complaint that a shop or larder is empty, making life tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop in the surface, but here it is a noun meaning a stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a secret stockpile, so it is a store of goods put by.

clue.text: You'll find quarters in time low-rise accommodation

indicators.note: in places the two compass points within the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
S and E are two quarters, or cardinal points, of the compass

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the cow's sound reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, the noise cattle make

explanation.surface: An advert for living space in a bungalow, with lodgings found in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-rise' looks like a building description, but it splits: 'low' is the cow's sound and 'rise' turns it upwards in this down clue, giving OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Houseroom is space or lodging in a home, as in refusing to give something houseroom.

clue.text: Accepted, after taking external entrance examination

indicators.note: after taking means the letter for accepted is taken inside the word for entrance

parts.note: an adit is a passage into a mine from outside, a way in from the surface
U is the abbreviation for upper-class and so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A candidate passes an entrance examination set by an outside body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'external' and 'entrance examination' suggest school admissions; the entrance is an ADIT, a mine's horizontal passage. U for socially acceptable is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection, especially of accounts.

clue.text: Angered, in a tizzy and upset

indicators.note: in a tizzy means flustered, so the letters of Angered are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is angry, flustered and upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or unhinge, as upset does.

clue.text: Be persuaded to recover

explanation.surface: Someone is talked into a view and gets well again.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round is both to change one's mind under persuasion and to regain consciousness or health.

clue.text: Fold note in case

indicators.note: in says the musical note goes inside the word case

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions to fold a note into its case.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is the line left by a fold in cloth or paper.

clue.text: The wrong 'medal given to me, right? It makes one sick

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of medal are put into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medal-winner complains that the award was a mistake and it sickens them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges only MEDAL, giving MALDE. Mal de mer is French for seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mal de mer, French for sea illness, is the nausea that comes with a ship's rolling.

clue.text: Soldiers, worn out, retreated

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
worn out means tired

explanation.surface: Exhausted troops fell back.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw or fall back, as an army does from a position.

clue.text: Manoeuvring group 'into destruction

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving about, so the letters of the next words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A military unit is steered towards ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprooting is tearing out by the roots, so it means wholesale destruction or eradication.

clue.text: Plot is overthrown — it is no credit to you

indicators.note: overthrown, in a down clue, means the word for plot is turned upside down

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A conspiracy has collapsed, and that does nobody any credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a conspiracy but is a flower bed, turned up in this down clue to give DEB. Both instances of 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is an entry recording money owed, the opposite of a credit in accounts.

clue.text: Submarine left to protect the bottom

parts.note: submarine as an adjective means beneath the sea

explanation.surface: A naval craft is left behind to guard the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' reads as a boat, but it is the adjective for anything below the waves. Underseal is a coating sprayed on a car's underside against rust.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, underseal means coating a vehicle's underside against corrosion, guarding its lowest surface.

clue.text: Most of the Bobby's beat

indicators.note: most of means the word the loses its final letter here

parts.note: Bobby is a pet form of Robert, and Rob is another

explanation.surface: Most of the British policeman's patrol route.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British policeman and his beat is his patrol, but here Bobby is a man's name: Bobby and Rob are both short for Robert. The final E of 'the' is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a regular pulse, the same sense as a heartbeat.

clue.text: Pine tree house, not at a resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, these words are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A forest hut stands away from a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' and 'tree' suggest a wood, but Pine is the definition, a verb. 'resort' reads as a holiday spot; split as re-sort, it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to yearn painfully, and eating one's heart out is the idiom for grieving or longing in silence.

clue.text: One who keeps quiet is a source of delight

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a very uncommunicative person, someone who clams up
from the saying that the world is one's shellfish to open, a thing offering pleasure and advantage

explanation.surface: A quiet, reserved person turns out to bring great joy.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish that clams shut gives a word for a tight-lipped person, and the saying about the world being yours makes it a fount of pleasure.

clue.text: Welcome support for something that cuts time off

indicators.note: support for means, in a down clue, that the greeting sits below the tool and holds it up

parts.note: a sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops
ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: A welcome prop for a cutting device that saves time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts time off' reads as saving time, but 'time off' is the definition. 'support for' puts AVE below SICKLE in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick leave is a period away from work allowed because of illness.

clue.text: It's leading article from first string

parts.note: head means foremost or first, as in head boy
a string is a line or cord

explanation.surface: A newspaper's main editorial taken from the very first line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading article' reads as a newspaper editorial, but the definition says only that this thing leads an article, sitting at its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the line of type at the top of a newspaper story, so it leads the article.

clue.text: In sympathy with strike, after 2/3 of men left

indicators.note: after means the striking piece follows the shortened men
two thirds of a three-letter word leaves two letters, here dropping the first letter of men

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Showing solidarity with industrial action once most of the workforce has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' reads as industrial action but is RAP, a knock. Port for left is from sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: En rapport, borrowed from French, means in close harmony or understanding with someone.

clue.text: According to one theory, heartless irascibility…

parts.note: as per means according to
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of theory are removed, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Some theory claims that bad temper comes from a lack of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the clue on into 18 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness of tone or temper, the sharpness of someone easily angered.

clue.text: Let alone, being considerably smaller

explanation.surface: A note that something is left alone because it has shrunk greatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means still less, used like 'never mind', and literally it is a far smaller amount.

clue.text: … without keeping one on, makes a female catty

indicators.note: keeping means the word for without holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: less means without, as in 'less sugar'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Not having one's temper kept in check makes a woman spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catty' reads as spiteful, but the definition is jokey: a female cat of the big kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is the female of the big cat, so a female member of the cat family.

clue.text: He can't choose the food in a pub

indicators.note: in says the item of food sits within the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
an egg is a basic food

explanation.surface: A diner in a pub cannot pick from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'beggars can't be choosers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says beggars can't be choosers: someone pleading for alms must take what is offered.

clue.text: Imprisoned in the end — about time!

indicators.note: in says the pieces for about and time sit inside the word end

parts.note: taken as written
C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A prisoner's release at last, after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'about time!' sounds like relief at a long-awaited release, but 'about' is C for circa and 'time' an age; 'in' places them inside the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Encaged is shut up as in a cage, so locked away or confined.

clue.text: Spirit used by tipsy chef

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drunken cook helps himself to the brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests drink for a tipsy chef, but it means the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, the inner self.

clue.text: Try harder to be more neatly dressed

explanation.surface: Advice to make more effort and smarten up one's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means make a greater effort, and literally it describes hoisting slack hosiery to look tidier.

clue.text: In favour of demonstration

parts.note: pro means in favour of
taken as written

explanation.surface: Supporting a public protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstration' suggests a protest, but it means evidence that shows something is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that establishes a fact, so a demonstration of truth.

clue.text: Rock music

explanation.surface: A two-word label for a style of popular music.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing is to sway or rock to and fro, and swing is also big-band jazz from the 1930s.

clue.text: Make speeches on relatively arcane topics — Egyptology, for starters

indicators.note: for starters means we take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A lecturer holds forth on obscure subjects, Egyptology to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal public address, often pompously.

clue.text: Noticing nothing wrong in disguise

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of Noticing are put in the wrong order

parts.note: nothing is zero, shown by the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone in disguise notices nothing amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' sits after 'nothing' but rearranges only the letters of Noticing, giving INCOGNIT, with O added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has concealed their identity, travelling under a false name or look.

clue.text: Ice-cap in sound? In this event, proceed as you think best

definitions.text: In this event, proceed as you think best

indicators.note: in sound tells us the words are said aloud and spelt as a different phrase

parts.note: ice as a verb means freeze, and a tile is British slang for a hat or cap

explanation.surface: A polar ice sheet in a stretch of sea, then advice to use your own judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a sea inlet beside the ice-cap, but it is the signal to say the words. Tile is old British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestyle race or contest lets each competitor choose their own technique or manner.

clue.text: One, perhaps, to appreciate appeal

parts.note: dig is slang for appreciate or like
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone might value a charitable appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One, perhaps' is a definition by example: 1 is a numeral. 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeral 1 is an example of a single figure from 0 to 9.
